title_candidates: OpenAI publishes its national-security AI rules
summary: OpenAI published national-security principles for government partnerships, including red lines around surveillance, autonomous weapons direction, and high-stakes automated decisions.

primary_source.title: Our approach to government and national security partnerships
primary_source.author: OpenAI
key_facts: OpenAI published National Security Principles for government and national-security partnerships.
The post says AI systems used in sensitive settings should reinforce democratic accountability, human judgment, and the rule of law.
OpenAI says its existing Department of War agreement includes restrictions on mass domestic surveillance, directing autonomous weapons systems, and high-stakes automated decisions.
OpenAI says it has Trusted Access for Cyber partnerships with several allied countries and EU institutions.
OpenAI says the highest-risk military uses of AI should be addressed through democratic and legislative processes, not by companies alone.

supporting_sources.title: Our agreement with the Department of War

prerequisites: A public-sector, vendor, school, or workplace AI policy to review

steps.instruction: Open OpenAI's principles and write down the three red-line areas it names.
Compare those red lines with any AI policy you use at work, school, or in a local organization.
Look for missing language on human approval, surveillance, autonomous action, and audit logs.
Ask your vendor or IT owner where model use is logged and who can approve sensitive deployments.
If the policy leaves high-stakes decisions to automation alone, flag it for legal, compliance, or leadership review.
